From colorful foliage and sprawling fall festivals to corn mazes, live music, spooky season attractions, and iconic NYC traditions, there’s no shortage of ways to make the most of the season.
Whether you’re looking to stay in the five boroughs or escape the concrete jungle for a day, these are the best things to do in NYC this fall.
Frolic through all the fall festivals and street fairs
Shutterstock / Felix Lipov
New York City–and its surrounding areas–come alive with fall festivals and fairs throughout September and October.

From seasonal bites and local finds to crisp-air strolls and the first pops of red and gold on the trees, there’s plenty of reason to get outside and soak up the season at these fall fairs and festivals:
New York City fairs & festivals:
Sept. 17–27: Feast of San Gennaro
Sept. 19: 2026 Bus Festival
Sept. 20–27: Brooklyn Book Festival
See NYC’s full fall street fair schedule here.
Fairs & festivals outside of NYC:
Sept. 17–20: Adirondack Balloon Festival
Sept. 18–Oct.: Autumn Glow Festival
Sept. 19–20: Warren County Hot Air Balloons, Fun & Games Festival
Sept. 20: Sleepy Hollow Street Fair
Sept. 26–27: Long Island Potato Festival
Sept. 26–27: Hudson Valley Garlic Festival
Oct. 4: Warwick Applefest
Pick fresh apples at these orchards near NYC
Source / Beak and Skiff Apple Orchards

Apple picking season is about to be in full swing, and dozens of dreamy farms near NYC are welcoming visitors for pick-your-own apples, hayrides, fresh-pressed cider, and those golden-hour photo ops that practically scream autumn!
Whether you’re craving a classic family outing, a romantic fall date, or just an excuse to load up on cider doughnuts, these are the best apple orchards near NYC to visit this season.
Make your evening glow with a Candlelight Concert
Source / Candlelight Concerts

Trade your usual night out for an evening surrounded by hundreds of flickering candles and live music at a Candlelight Concert in NYC. From classical masterpieces to tributes to some of your favorite artists, these intimate concerts make for a seriously memorable night out.
See the full list of upcoming Candlelight concerts in NYC and grab tickets here.
Grab your dirndl and lederhosen and head to the 69th German-American Steuben Parade
Source / German-American Steuben Parade
Fifth Avenue – Upper East Side

For a classic fall NYC spectacle, head to Manhattan’s Upper East Side on Saturday, September 19, 2026, when the 69th annual German-American Steuben Parade takes over the neighborhood with a parade kickoff on Fifth Avenue and an Oktoberfest afterparty in Central Park.
Expect traditional floats, marching bands, and large crowds in Bavarian dress.
Stock up on your favorite Halloween treats at NYC’s oldest candy shop

108 Rivington Street
Economy Candy is a Lower East Side institution that has been satisfying New Yorkers’ sweet tooth since 1937—long before candy shops started taking over your TikTok feed.

Today, the family-owned Rivington Street shop stocks 2,500 different types of confections from around the world, including plenty of nostalgic, hard-to-find candies you probably haven’t seen since you were a kid.
Whether you’re hunting for Halloween treats or just want to relive your childhood in candy form, this old-school sweet shop is worth a stop.
Step behind the tape at this chilling true crime experience
Source / Mind of a Serial Killer: The Experience
526 6th Avenue

If you’re looking for something a little darker than your typical NYC outing, step behind the police tape at Mind of a Serial Killer: The Experience, a massive immersive true crime exhibition in Manhattan.

Explore real artifacts, recreated crime scenes, FBI profiling, and a VR investigation as you dive into some of history’s most notorious cases—including Ted Bundy and Jeffrey Dahmer. It’s definitely not your average immersive experience, and graphic content means it’s best suited for mature audiences.
Watch giant balloons take over NYC at the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade
Shutterstock / Ryan Rahman

Kick off the holiday season the very New York way at the 100th annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Thursday, November 26. Watch larger-than-life balloons, dazzling floats, marching bands, and live performances make their way through Manhattan before the parade wraps up at Macy’s Herald Square.

And this year is a particularly big one: the centennial celebration will feature a record-breaking 100 inflatable elements, including new and returning character balloons—and yes, Snoopy is coming back as Joe Cool.
Grab a Signature Slice during NYC’s inaugural Pizza Week
Shutterstock / James Andrews1

If your ideal fall plan involves carbs, add New York City’s inaugural Pizza Week to your calendar: it runs September 20–October 4, 2026, featuring exclusive Signature Slices at 23 independent pizzerias across Manhattan, Brooklyn, and Queens.
No tickets or reservations are required—pay per slice and text a rating to help choose the citywide Best Slice, with a portion of proceeds benefiting Slice Out Hunger.
Shop all your Halloween essentials at Spirit Halloween
Shutterstock / rblfmr

‘Tis the season for a trip to Spirit Halloween in search of the perfect costume and spooky decor. Whether you’re going full spooky or keeping things scare-free, the Halloween megastore has costumes, décor, accessories, and plenty of other seasonal finds to get you ready for October 31.
And good news for New Yorkers: locations are popping up all over the city, so you won’t have to travel too far to get your Halloween fix. Find your closest store.
See St. Patrick’s Cathedral in a whole new light at LUMINISCENCE
Source / LUMINISCENCE
St. Patrick’s Cathedral – 5th Avenue
Step inside St. Patrick’s Cathedral for a one-of-a-kind evening of 360-degree light projections, live orchestral music, and storytelling this fall.

The immersive 60-minute experience will transform the iconic cathedral’s soaring Gothic Revival interiors with vibrant projections, while a live orchestra, choir, and narration from The Chosen star Jonathan Roumie bring the building’s history to life.
It’s a pretty spectacular way to experience one of NYC’s most famous landmarks after dark.
Chase NYC’s best fall foliage at these standout spots
Shutterstock / Songquan Deng

You don’t have to leave the five boroughs to get your fill of crimson leaves, golden trees, and peak fall vibes. Once autumn rolls in, NYC’s parks and gardens become their own colorful escape from the concrete jungle.
Here are a few standout spots to add to your fall bucket list:
Central Park: Wander the Mall, The Ramble, and around the Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir for some of the city’s best leafy scenery
Fort Tryon Park: Head uptown for sweeping Hudson River views surrounded by colorful trees, especially around the Heather Garden and Cloisters area
Prospect Park: Brooklyn’s sprawling green space brings plenty of fall color, with especially pretty views around the Ravine, Long Meadow, and lake
Van Cortlandt Park: Escape to the Bronx for wooded trails and plenty of foliage without actually leaving the city
Inwood Hill Park: Hike through one of Manhattan’s last remaining natural forests for a much more wild-feeling fall outing
Wave Hill: This Bronx garden overlooking the Hudson turns especially dreamy in autumn, with landscaped gardens, mature trees, and river views
…Then experience even more stunning fall foliage just outside NYC
Source / ROOST

When the leaves start putting on their annual show, you don’t have to travel halfway across the country to see it. These scenic spots just outside NYC make for easy fall escapes, with winding roads, historic estates, and plenty of colorful foliage to take in.

Take a scenic road trip through America’s No. 1 fall foliage destination: Head north to the Adirondacks, recently crowned the country’s top destination for fall foliage, and cruise along the winding High Peaks Scenic Byway that offers some seriously spectacular autumn views

Explore a historic Hudson Valley estate framed by fall color: Just about 2 hours from Manhattan, Olana State Historic Site is a 250-acre estate overlooking the Hudson River. Wander its five miles of historic carriage roads, take in sweeping views of the Catskill Mountains and Hudson River, and follow trails around its 10-acre lake
Attend NYC’s best Halloween events
Getty Images / GummyBone
The spookiest time of the year is upon us, and NYC is celebrating to the fullest.
From haunted houses and Halloween parties to spooky parades and over-the-top decorations, there’s no shortage of ways to get into the spirit around the city.
Whether you’re looking for a proper scare, a family-friendly celebration, or simply an excuse to dress up and roam the city, NYC has something spooky in store this Halloween.
Sing along to these iconic pop hits with a Broadway twist
Source / Katy Beth Barber – Kbarberphotography
This fall, Broadway Sings is bringing the songs of ABBA, Whitney Houston, and Fleetwood Mac to life with a theatrical spin at The Cutting Room.

Hear Broadway performers take on ABBA classics like “Dancing Queen,” Whitney Houston power ballads and Fleetwood Mac favorites like “Landslide” and “Rhiannon,” all backed by a 15-piece live orchestra.
With limited performances throughout September and October, these intimate concerts are a fun excuse to belt out some legendary hits.
Grab tickets below:
Sept. 17 & Oct. 17: ABBA
Oct. 9: Whitney Houston
Sept. 23 & Oct. 24: Fleetwood Mac
Stop by Cj Hendry’s Rockefeller Center Flower Market for an everlasting bouquet
Add caption
Rockefeller Center Plaza – 30 Rockefeller Plaza
If you’re looking for a can’t-miss fall pop-up in NYC, Cj Hendry’s viral Flower Market is returning to Rockefeller Center this September.

From September 24 through 27, 2026, the larger-than-life floral playground is transforming the iconic plaza with interactive art, NYC-native blooms, and a free flower for every single guest. The best part: it’s free and open to the public!
Get lost in a giant corn maze
Facebook / Queens County Farm Museum
Put your sense of direction to the test at one of the many sprawling corn mazes just outside NYC this fall.

From NYC’s only corn maze at Queens County Farm Museum to a 10-acre labyrinth in New Jersey, these farms turn their fields into winding autumn adventures filled with hidden clues, puzzles, themed paths, and plenty of chances to get deliciously lost.
Many also have pumpkin picking, hayrides, apple cider donuts, and other fall activities to make a full day of it. See the full list.

Step inside 15 immersive rooms at this NYC art museum
Source / Mercer Labs
Mercer Labs – 21 Dey Street
See art in a whole new way at Mercer Labs, where classic masterpieces meet cutting-edge technology, interactive installations, and immersive soundscapes across 15 rooms in Downtown Manhattan.

Walk through a 500,000-LED hologram, explore a room filled with pink hydrangeas, feel the floor vibrate with 4DSOUND, and even play the cello with robotic arms. It’s part art museum, part futuristic playground—and definitely not your typical museum visit.

Cheer on thousands of runners at the NYC Marathon
Source / TCS New York City Marathon
One of NYC’s biggest fall traditions returns on Sunday, November 1, as the TCS New York City Marathon takes over all five boroughs.
The 2026 race marks the 50th anniversary of the iconic five-borough course, with nearly 60,000 runners expected to make the 26.2-mile trek from Staten Island to Central Park.

You don’t have to be running to join the fun: line the streets with fellow New Yorkers, cheer on the runners, catch the elite athletes, and soak up the electric energy that takes over the city every November.
This year’s professional field includes three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, and 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists.
Catch the Knicks’ championship banner-raising home opener
CJ GUNTHER / Shutterstock
Madison Square Garden
Basketball season is almost back, and this year’s Knicks home opener is a particularly big one.

On October 20, the team will face the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden for the first game of the 2026–27 regular season—and before tipoff, the Knicks will raise their first championship banner since 1973 after winning the NBA title last season.
The night will also mark LeBron James’ first game as a 76er, making for a pretty stacked way to kick off the new NBA season in New York.
Head to an outdoor fall concert
Source / Global Citizen Festival
Once the temperatures cool down, there’s no better way to spend a day outdoors than with live music.
From a stacked three-day festival in Queens to a massive free concert in Central Park, these fall shows bring some seriously big names to NYC.

Dance along to 18 artists at All Things Go: The beloved music festival is taking over Forest Hills Stadium from September 25–27, bringing Zara Larsson, Brandi Carlile, MUNA, Carly Rae Jepsen, Lola Young, Rebecca Black, and more to Queens for three days of live music

See Ms. Lauryn Hill, Lenny Kravitz, and more for a good cause: Head to Central Park on September 26 for the 2026 Global Citizen Festival, featuring Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean, Lenny Kravitz, John Legend, Lainey Wilson, Shaboozey, and TOMORROW X TOGETHER (TXT)
Escape into a surreal world at this immersive NYC art museum
Source / Arte Museum New York
Celebrate Arte Museum New York’s first birthday this September with special ticket prices and a journey through 14 mesmerizing digital art installations.

Step inside a world of cascading waterfalls, crashing waves, mythical creatures, and dreamy landscapes, all brought to life through vivid visuals, sound, and scent. You can also wander through digital versions of works by Monet and Van Gogh and unwind with a tea at the immersive ARTE CAFE.
And through September 30, you can snag the lowest ticket price to experience it for yourself.
Grab a meal or drinks at NYC’s newest restaurants and bars
Source / Galo
Now that the worst of the summer heat is finally easing up, we can actually go outside again without immediately sweating through our clothes.
Naturally, the city’s dining scene is keeping pace, with a fresh slew of bars and restaurants making their debut.
From breezy sidewalk spots to buzzy new hotspots already vying for a spot on your group chat’s dinner rotation, there are plenty of new places to eat, drink, and linger. Find our lists below:
August New Restaurants & Bars
September New Restaurants & Bars
Feast on unlimited sushi at this massive NYC festival
Source / SUSHI-CON 2025
Pier 36 – 299 South Street

Calling all sushi lovers: SUSHI-CON 2026 is taking over Pier 36 on October 11, bringing more than 60 exhibitors from Japan, the U.S., and around the world for one seriously stacked day of Japanese food and culture. Your ticket gets you unlimited tastings of bluefin tuna, uni, caviar, scallops, salmon, A5 Wagyu, matcha, yuzu, and more.
The main event? A 400+ pound live Bluefin tuna cutting show, where expert sushi chefs will carve the massive fish right before your eyes before serving up fresh otoro, chutoro, and akami.
Get a head start on holiday season happenings
Source / Rockefeller Center
New York City is apparently skipping right over fall and looking ahead the most wonderful time of the year, announcing the return of some of the city’s most classic holiday happenings.
If you’d like to get a head start on the festive season, we have just the plans for you:
Oct. 10: Rockefeller Center’s iconic Ice Rink opens for the season
Oct. 28: Bryant Park’s Bank of America Winter Village returns
Nov. 18: Fifth Avenue’s massive 30-foot wide snowflake is lit for the season

Cheer on thousands of runners at the NYC Marathon

Source / TCS New York City Marathon

One of NYC’s biggest fall traditions returns on Sunday, November 1, as the TCS New York City Marathon takes over all five boroughs.


The 2026 race marks the 50th anniversary of the iconic five-borough course, with nearly 60,000 runners expected to make the 26.2-mile trek from Staten Island to Central Park.


You don’t have to be running to join the fun: line the streets with fellow New Yorkers, cheer on the runners, catch the elite athletes, and soak up the electric energy that takes over the city every November.


This year’s professional field includes three defending champions, 40 Olympians and Paralympians, and 25 Olympic, Paralympic, and World Championships medalists.

Catch the Knicks’ championship banner-raising home opener

CJ GUNTHER / Shutterstock

Madison Square Garden

Basketball season is almost back, and this year’s Knicks home opener is a particularly big one.


On October 20, the team will face the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden for the first game of the 2026–27 regular season—and before tipoff, the Knicks will raise their first championship banner since 1973 after winning the NBA title last season.


The night will also mark LeBron James’ first game as a 76er, making for a pretty stacked way to kick off the new NBA season in New York.

Head to an outdoor fall concert

Source / Global Citizen Festival

Once the temperatures cool down, there’s no better way to spend a day outdoors than with live music.


From a stacked three-day festival in Queens to a massive free concert in Central Park, these fall shows bring some seriously big names to NYC.

Dance along to 18 artists at All Things Go: The beloved music festival is taking over Forest Hills Stadium from September 25–27, bringing Zara Larsson, Brandi Carlile, MUNA, Carly Rae Jepsen, Lola Young, Rebecca Black, and more to Queens for three days of live music


See Ms. Lauryn Hill, Lenny Kravitz, and more for a good cause: Head to Central Park on September 26 for the 2026 Global Citizen Festival, featuring Ms. Lauryn Hill & Wyclef Jean, Lenny Kravitz, John Legend, Lainey Wilson, Shaboozey, and TOMORROW X TOGETHER (TXT)


Escape into a surreal world at this immersive NYC art museum

Source / Arte Museum New York

Celebrate Arte Museum New York’s first birthday this September with special ticket prices and a journey through 14 mesmerizing digital art installations.


Step inside a world of cascading waterfalls, crashing waves, mythical creatures, and dreamy landscapes, all brought to life through vivid visuals, sound, and scent. You can also wander through digital versions of works by Monet and Van Gogh and unwind with a tea at the immersive ARTE CAFE.


And through September 30, you can snag the lowest ticket price to experience it for yourself.

Feast on unlimited sushi at this massive NYC festival

Source / SUSHI-CON 2025

Pier 36 – 299 South Street

Calling all sushi lovers: SUSHI-CON 2026 is taking over Pier 36 on October 11, bringing more than 60 exhibitors from Japan, the U.S., and around the world for one seriously stacked day of Japanese food and culture. Your ticket gets you unlimited tastings of bluefin tuna, uni, caviar, scallops, salmon, A5 Wagyu, matcha, yuzu, and more.


The main event? A 400+ pound live Bluefin tuna cutting show, where expert sushi chefs will carve the massive fish right before your eyes before serving up fresh otoro, chutoro, and akami.

Get a head start on holiday season happenings

Source / Rockefeller Center

New York City is apparently skipping right over fall and looking ahead the most wonderful time of the year, announcing the return of some of the city’s most classic holiday happenings.


If you’d like to get a head start on the festive season, we have just the plans for you:

Oct. 10: Rockefeller Center’s iconic Ice Rink opens for the season


Oct. 28: Bryant Park’s Bank of America Winter Village returns


Nov. 18: Fifth Avenue’s massive 30-foot wide snowflake is lit for the season
